Definition: from G303 and a derivative of G3501; to renovate, i.e. reform:--renew.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: 'And be renewed in the spirit of your mind.' It is the renewing of the mind itself — not new information, but a mind made new in its spirit, the way of thinking itself changed, so that the new man can be put on.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for being renewed in the mind carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the command — be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and the new man follows.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
